name: Pastel Parchment
lede: Pastel Parchment is a soft, warm tan, a 1927 fashion-dictionary name from the trade era when dressmakers and milliners needed a shared color vocabulary.

sections.title: A fashion-trade tan
sections.body:
The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 dates this name to 1927 and plots it on plate 11 A 5 [1]. A near-duplicate name from the same source, Rose Nude, was recorded one year later, in 1928, at a nearly identical spot on the chart, a sign of how closely the fashion trade's color vocabulary could overlap [1]. Who first used "parchment" for this tan, or why "pastel" was added, is undocumented in the books we hold [1].

Its Munsell notation is 7.5YR 7.4/4.3, and the closest of our common colors is [[tan]], only 3.6 units away [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this tan appears in 1,648, about 6.9 percent, more common than 90 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 96 of 1,674 paintings, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.4 times the expected rate [2].

[[painter:raphael|Raphael]] is its most devoted painter, present in 8 of 36 works here, 4.1 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is a 1000 painting, nine centuries before the 1927 name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named tan, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[bisque]] and [[fawn-color]] [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a fashion-trade name evoking parchment paper
